metadata.title: International Computer and Information Literacy Study Assessment Framework

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an ICILS assessment framework rather than an empirical analysis of ICILS micro-data. It describes how the computer and information literacy (CIL) construct is structured, how test items and student/context instruments are mapped to the framework, and how the assessment is designed. Because no analytic dataset, sampling frame, or estimation procedure is implemented here, there is no reported use of complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights or replicate weights). For any later empirical ICILS analyses using the ICILS student and school data, analysts should apply the ICILS sampling weights and replicate weights provided with the international database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the complex design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design document that does not estimate student achievement models or produce PV-based outcomes from ICILS micro-data. As a result, plausible values handling and missing-data handling strategies are not part of the reported methodology in this text. Any PV generation and missing-data procedures would be implemented in the subsequent ICILS assessment administration and scoring/estimation pipeline, not in this framework description.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used for assessment design and instrument specification; no analytic student sample is defined in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This document specifies the ICILS computer and information literacy (CIL) construct and the assessment framework used to design the ICILS test and contextual instruments. It outlines the purpose of the study, positions CIL relative to traditional disciplines, and defines the CIL construct through strands and aspects, including a contextual framework with contextual levels and variables. The assessment design section describes the ICILS test design, the types of assessment tasks, and how test items are mapped to the CIL framework. Because the text provided is a framework description, it does not report an empirical model, predictive performance, or achievement benchmarks derived from student data. Therefore, no ML-based results or PV/missing-data estimation choices are evaluated within this document.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided material is an assessment framework (instrument and construct specification) rather than an empirical study that trains or evaluates ML models on ICILS student micro-data. Consequently, there is no reported analytic sample size, no country-level sample breakdown, no PV estimation strategy, and no missing-data handling procedure tied to model estimation. The extraction is sparse by design because the document focuses on defining and mapping the CIL construct to assessment tasks and questionnaires, not on reporting predictive outcomes.
